# Orchestrate: Monitoring, Integration, Close, and Resume

## Step 4: Monitor and broker

Workers and DAs collaborate directly on the shared swarm board using `@mentions` (`@da-1`, `@worker-1`, `@coordinator`). Idle members stay asleep in `waiting` state at zero token cost until mentioned. You wait. Do not poll `swarm(action: "status")` in a loop or send "are you done?" posts.

Antigravity wakes you automatically when a member mentions `@coordinator` — end your turn (call no more tools) after spawning to wait for notifications. Two kinds of board traffic matter:

- **Waiting turns.** Workers ending a turn with `WAITING worker-N: round R sent to da-M` (without mentioning `@coordinator`) are sleeping while their DA reviews, not DONE. Do not interrupt them.
- **`@coordinator` posts.** These are your events. Act only on a message whose first line is one of these:

| First line | Meaning | Your action |
|---|---|---|
| `DONE worker-N` | DA returned PASS, or a wording-only REVISE the worker applied as notes; or, on a stream whose review is `none`, its checks passed | Record it with `append DONE` (below). Check the write set was respected. On a `none` stream, hold the acceptance output in the DONE against the subtask's acceptance lines and run the quick ones again yourself; a check that does not hold goes back to the worker as a new round, and you log its `PLAN` again. A PASS is final: never send a DONE back for a note the worker already applied. If the worker used `workspace: "inherit"` and is no longer needed, stop it with `swarm(action: "kill", name: "worker-N")` and log `append RELEASE worker-N` (if it used `workspace: "share"`, land/merge its branch first before killing!). Kill a DA the same way once `releasable` lists it and none of its passed work is still open to change (Follow-ups, below). |
| `BRIEF worker-N: GAP` (from a DA) | The subtask as written would not give the user what they asked for, or drops one of their rules | Read each gap against the user's words it quotes. For one that holds, correct the subtask and send it to worker-N whole, first line `SUBTASK worker-N (corrected; it replaces the first)`, and log its `PLAN` again; ask the user instead when the gap is in the goal itself. For one that does not, tell the DA why in one line. `BRIEF worker-N: OK` needs no action. |
| `SPLIT worker-N` | The worker's design has 3 or more parts that can be built at the same time | Check each part as you would a stream entry (Step 1): a testable goal, an acceptance check from the world, a one-agent line, and a write set inside worker-N's that overlaps no other part. Send a part that fails back to worker-N to fix or keep, and spawn the parts that pass now: one worker per part under the next unused indices, with a subtask made from its part line, the `Design` line, and the `Interfaces` line as inputs, and no findings, so it builds without redesigning. Give each to a DA with fewer than 3 workers (spawn one if none has room) and tell that DA, as in Reassignment in `references/protocol.md`. In one `append --stdin`, log worker-N's `PLAN` again with its kept write set (once more if a returned part changes it) and one `PLAN` per new worker with `split from worker-N`. A part that must wait for a shared resource or an agent slot spawns when that frees; log each `PLAN` when its worker spawns. A respawn of worker-N gets its Keep part, not the whole stream. Reply to worker-N only to rule otherwise. |
| `ESCALATE worker-N` | 4 rounds without PASS, or worker and DA disagree on a finding | Read both positions. Rule on it, or re-scope the subtask inside the goal yourself. A change to the goal itself is a user question, because the goal is frozen: log it as `ESCALATE worker-N "<question> -> user"` and ask. Do not let it loop further. |
| `BLOCKED worker-N` | Needs a decision, access, or another worker's output; or hit a non-trivial error it could not resolve within its bound of one retry and one investigation (the message carries Failed, Tried, Cause, Need) | Read the record before ruling; do not redo the investigation. Cause inside the goal: answer, grant the path, or re-scope the subtask. Cause in another worker's piece: route it there as a new round. Cause in the plan or the goal itself: a user question. Log one line: `append BLOCKED worker-N "<cause> -> <ruling>"`. |
| `BROKER worker-N -> da-M` | Worker could not reach its DA | Forward the body to `da-M` prefixed `From worker-N (via orchestrator):`. Keep relaying until DONE. |
| `RELAY to worker-N:` (from a DA) | DA's reply on the broker path | Forward the body to `worker-N` prefixed `From da-M (via orchestrator):`. |
| `ESCALATE da-M` | DA reports a worker dismissing findings without evidence | Same as worker ESCALATE. |

**Log each event you act on, once.** A `DONE` line's text is `r<R> PASS`, then a `|` and the worker's `Rounds:` summary, copied; on a stream whose review is `none` it is `r0 CHECKS`, then a `|` and the checks that passed. In the same turn, copy the report's `Paths created` line, when it lists any, into the plan file's `Paths created` section. A `BLOCKED` or `ESCALATE` gets one line recording your ruling. `INTEGRATE`, each `REVIEW`, and `CLOSE` are your own lines, with actor `team-lead`; a `RESPAWN` line's actor is the dead worker. Heartbeats and brokered traffic are not events and get no line.

Silence means work in progress. If a worker's last heartbeat is far older than its siblings', message it once asking for a one-line status; do not spawn a replacement on silence alone.

**Provider failures and quota limits.** If a member stalls on quota or capacity and enters `waiting`, switch its model in-place with `swarm(action: "model", name: "worker-N", model: "<alternate from swarm models>")` (stating why) — it keeps its conversation and resumes without losing work. If a member permanently fails or is `killed`, spawn a replacement under the **next unused index** (`worker-7`, never a reused name) with the same subtask plus a note naming files the dead worker may have touched, notify `@da-M`, and log `append RESPAWN <old> "-> <new> | <reason>"`.

**Rebalancing.** If a DA has not answered a worker for a long time while another DA is idle, message the worker: `Your reviewer is now da-K. Resend your current brief there.` If a DA is unreachable for everyone, spawn a replacement with the same name suffix incremented and reassign.

**Follow-ups go back to the same DA.** When work a DA already passed changes again (a note from the user, a comment on a posted change, a fix round), send the change to that DA as the next round. It already holds the verified facts; a new DA has to rebuild them and can contradict the earlier PASS. Spawn a new DA only for new work, or when the first one is gone.

**When the user adds a bar or changes a decision.** Write it in the plan file's `User rules` section, verbatim, and send it in the same turn to every open worker and DA (the `RULE` message in `references/protocol.md`). It applies from that moment to every stream it touches: a worker measuring or building against a setting the user has replaced moves to the new one, because results on the old setting answer a question nobody is asking any more. Put it in every later subtask and DA prompt.

**When a result calls for a next step.** A DONE whose result points at more work inside the goal (a reviewed recommendation to apply, a fix a finding implies) becomes a new stream now: write its entry, spawn it, and tell the user what started. Ask first only before an irreversible or production-facing step.

**You do not fix worker code.** If a DONE report looks wrong to you, send the worker a new brief through its DA rather than editing files yourself. The moment you edit, you become an unreviewed worker.

## Step 5: Integrate

When every worker in the wave reports DONE, check the pieces fit: run the top-level build or test command, and confirm no file outside any write set changed (`git status` / `git diff --stat`). Log the result: `append INTEGRATE team-lead "<result>"`. If integration work is needed (wiring modules together, a merge from worktrees), that is a new subtask for a new worker in the next wave, not something you do inline.

Start the next wave if there is one.

## Step 6: Final review

Run this step only when a seam spans workers: a stream was split, or one worker's change depends on another's (a later wave, a shared interface, a file two workers changed). Unrelated streams have no seam, and each stream's own PASS or checks closed it, so go to Step 7.

Send one DA the whole-goal brief in `references/protocol.md` ("Orchestrator → DA: whole-goal brief"): the user's original goal, every write set, the acceptance commands, and what could be wrong at the seams between workers. Individual PASSes prove parts; this proves the whole. Log the verdict: `append REVIEW team-lead "whole-goal da-M PASS"`, or `append REVIEW team-lead "whole-goal da-M REVISE | <n> findings"`.

On REVISE, spawn a fresh worker for each finding under the next unused index, with the owning worker's write set and the finding, reviewed by the DA that passed the owner's work when it is still live (`swarm(action: "status")`), otherwise by another live DA. Log one line per worker: `append PLAN worker-N "-> da-M | fix: <finding summary> | <acceptance>"`. Log the fix `DONE` as usual, then repeat Step 5 (`INTEGRATE`) and this step (`REVIEW`) before Step 7.

A whole-goal PASS is final. Notes attached to it (wording, labels, a commit message) go to one fresh worker under the next unused index, reviewed by the DA that ran the whole-goal review, which checks only that each note was applied; there is no whole-goal re-review. Log it in the same `append --stdin` as the `REVIEW` line, as `PLAN worker-N "-> da-M | notes: <summary> | <acceptance>"`, so `releasable` keeps that DA until the notes worker's DONE. A REVISE whose findings are all wording-only is a PASS with notes: log it as PASS and handle it the same way.

## Step 7: Report and shut down

Close the log with one stopping word (`skills/pave-init/references/pave-spec.md` §9.13): `append CLOSE team-lead "<word> | <one-line summary>"`. A produced report is not acceptance, so pick the word that is true:

- `accepted` — every review a stream named PASSed, the whole-goal review PASSed if Step 6 ran, and the acceptance checks hold.
- `closed_unaccepted` — work stopped with an honest result that did not pass.
- `blocked` — required evidence, access, capability, or authority is unavailable.
- `incomplete` — required work remains open, including a run you abandon.
- `exhausted` — the useful approaches are used up.

Tell the user, in this order: the stopping word, leading the report, with the verdict for the whole goal; then one line per stream, named by its subject, with its result and its Speed line; then deferred items and anything you had to decide on their behalf. Name streams by subject in everything the user reads, here and in status updates: `worker-N`, `da-M`, and round counts are addresses and bookkeeping for the log, and the user has never seen them. An `accepted` close needs no go from the user: if this run was one step of a larger task and the next step is reversible and touches nothing live, start it and say what started. Ask first only before an irreversible or production-facing step.

Before you release the team, remove what the run built only to do its work: the paths in the plan file's `Paths created` section (build output, caches, scratch files, finished worktrees). Keep branches, evidence, and any tree with uncommitted changes, and tell the user what you removed. Then release the team: land/merge any `workspace: "share"` branches first (killing deletes a share workspace), then call `swarm(action: "kill", name: "<name>")` for each remaining agent `append CLOSE` names and log `append RELEASE <name>`.

## When the work is a document people read

A handoff, a design, a results page, or a runbook is read later by people who were not in the session. For such a deliverable these rules are part of its goal, stated in the brief or not. They do not cover a reply or a status report to the user, a commit message, or instructions written for an agent.

- **Explain it the way you would to a colleague.** Write full sentences in everyday words that connect cause and effect. Tell the reader directly what to do. Name each person, the user included, and say only what your sources show that person did, decided, or said: never an intent, a promise, or a decision they do not show. Write "I" for the user only when the brief asks for the user's voice. A gap in your sources is your gap, not a person's: say what is not known and whom to ask, never that someone does not know it. No clipped fragments such as "Prod: not checked.", and no chat shorthand such as "&" or "w/".
- **Outline first.** Open with a short summary, then what the reader must do, then how. A page that teaches a method ends with a worked example. Long commands, lists of IDs, and links go in an appendix.
- **Say the action in the heading.** "Step 3. Roll the new build in beta", not "Rollout considerations".
- **Lead each bullet with a bold label**, then one or two sentences.
- **Use real names.** Use the same few names throughout, and say what each one is in the sentence that first uses it. Find out what a name means before you use it. When you cannot, keep the data under that name and say once that your sources do not define it. Do not coin a label for a thing, and do not add a glossary.
- **Keep tables for tabular data.** Exact numbers go in the table, notes go under it as bullets, and reasons go in prose.
- **Keep the IDs the reader needs**, in backticks. One that a step uses goes in that step, and one that lets the reader find or check a thing goes in an appendix table. Leave out line numbers, run numbers, agent names, and file paths the reader cannot open. When the reader needs something that exists only on the author's machine, write the step that gets it to them.
- **Leave your working material out.** Source keys, tags such as "unverified", play-by-play, stale status, and lists of hosts, caveats, or open questions stay in your notes. What changes how the reader acts stays on the page, as one plain sentence in front of the step it affects: a part you did not verify, a real limit, a condition, or whose approval the step needs.
- **List sources once, at the end.** Each one is something the reader can open. Say so when a number has no copy the reader can reach.
- **Keep it short.** Cut the prose to about half the first draft and keep the data, the steps, and the conditions on them. Link at most one companion page.
- **Check it before you hand it over.** Check each number against its source, read the live state again for anything the page calls current, or give the date you read it when you cannot, and read the page once from the top as its reader. Then go through your sources once more for every instruction to wait or stop, every warning, every check nobody has run, and every approval still owed: each one that changes what the reader does is on the page, in front of the step it affects.
- **Edit a published page in place.** Once the user has edited a published page by hand, that page is the truth: never publish an older copy over it.

Before: `Deploy: blocked. Cause: stale pin (see notes, section 6). Owner: TBD.`
After: The deploy is blocked because the config still points at the old build. Update the pin, then run the deploy again.

## Resume

After a context rebuild (compaction, a resumed session, or the goal-restate hook firing), rebuild your state from the log, not from memory:

1. Run `python3 $SKILL/scripts/orchestrate_log.py --runtime antigravity status`. It prints the goal, one line per subtask, and the log's last line. Then read the plan file's `User rules` section: a restate of the goal carries every bar there, each with its current number or `not measured yet`.
2. Run `swarm(action: "status")`. An open worker may be a first-round subtask or one in a Step 6 fix round. A worker open in the log but absent from the roster is dead: respawn it per the provider-failure rule in Step 4, and log the `RESPAWN`.
3. Continue from the last line. Do not re-plan or re-spawn a subtask `status` shows as DONE. With no `PLAN` line yet, Step 1 is unfinished: continue it from `<run id>.plan`.

After starting a new conversation (which rotates `ANTIGRAVITY_CONVERSATION_ID`), `status` finds no run for this conversation and prints the `adopt` command for the orphaned log. Run `adopt <log>` first, then the steps above. Note that `stopped` swarm members from before a restart revive automatically when `@mentioned` on the board; only `killed` members need a respawn.

## Hooks

The plugin registers three hooks in `<PLUGIN_ROOT>/hooks.json` via `hooks/ag_hook_adapter.py` (`SessionStart`, `PostToolUse`, and `PostInvocation`). Because Antigravity `PostToolUse` cannot inject context directly, `PostToolUse` evaluates the canonical hooks and spools any reminder per `conversationId`, which `PostInvocation` drains and injects as a `systemMessage` right before the next model turn. All three hooks never block and fail open. `ORCHESTRATE_PYTHON` sets the interpreter they use.

- **Goal restate** (`SessionStart`) fires when a conversation owning an open run (`~/.orchestrate/active-<ANTIGRAVITY_CONVERSATION_ID>`) starts or resumes (fresh conversations with no active marker stay silent; Antigravity does not emit a separate `compact` event). It asks you to restate the goal from the log header and every bar and rule in `<run id>.plan`, run `status` and `swarm(action: "status")`, name each open subtask, and name the fewest steps to `CLOSE`. Answer it with Resume.
- **Speed-up question** (`PostToolUse` on `run_command` → `PostInvocation`) fires after a log write whose last line is `PLAN`, `DONE`, `BLOCKED`, `ESCALATE`, `RESPAWN`, or `INTEGRATE`, at most once a minute (`ORCHESTRATE_SPEEDUP_SECONDS`). It asks whether anything else can overlap, parallelize, or be cut, asks you to hand off work you lack context for, and asks you to kill finished agents no longer needed (after landing any `share` workspace).
- **Maintainer reminder** (`PostToolUse` on `write_file|edit_file|write_to_file|replace_file_content` → `PostInvocation`) fires only inside `orchestrate-worker` conversations (identified by `SUBTASK worker-` on line 1 of the initial brief and absence of a lead marker), at most once a minute (`ORCHESTRATE_SEAT_SECONDS`). You have nothing to answer.

There is no Stop hook. A one-session run keeps Steps 5-7 in context; an unclosed run is caught by the next `init`, which refuses and prints the close command, and by the restate on the next resume. `append CLOSE` prints a one-line reminder naming every agent not logged as released.

## Anti-patterns

- **Doing "just this one small piece" yourself.** It skips review and desynchronizes your plan from the files.
- **Designing a stream yourself.** The worker who builds a stream designs it. A lead design merges unrelated asks into one plan and makes every worker wait for it.
- **Overlapping write sets.** Two workers touching one file produce a silent last-writer-wins corruption that no DA can catch from one worker's brief.
- **Vague goals.** "Improve the auth module" cannot be PASSed or failed. "Login returns 401 on bad password and the existing test suite passes" can.
- **Mentioning `@coordinator` on routine worker-to-DA traffic.** Every `@coordinator` mention wakes the lead and fills its context. Worker-to-DA briefs and verdicts mention only `@da-M` or `@worker-N`.
- **Killing a `workspace: "share"` worker before landing its changes.** `swarm(action: "kill")` permanently deletes a `share` workspace. Merge or copy its work first.
- **Killing a quota-limited worker instead of switching its model.** Use `swarm(action: "model", ...)` on a `waiting` worker to preserve its conversation and work.
- **Treating silence as failure.** Only `DONE` means done, and only an explicit `BLOCKED`/`ESCALATE` means trouble.
- **Fixing beyond findings.** When brokering, forward verbatim. Do not edit the DA's findings or the worker's rebuttal.
- **Cutting scope to finish sooner.** Speeding up means removing waste and running more at once. A stream the user asked for leaves the run only on the user's word or a stop rule the user set; a build or report with part of the work is a checkpoint, and you call it one.

## Reference files

- `references/subtask.md` — the worker subtask template; fill it once per stream or split part.
- `references/protocol.md` — DA spawn prompt, message formats, the whole-goal brief, broker fallback, reassignment.
- `references/model-seats.md` — how to pick models from `swarm(action: "models")` and switch models on quota limits.
- `swarm(action: "models")` and `/hooks` — live model/quota check and hook inspection before spawning.
- `scripts/orchestrate_log.py` — the run log; `init`, `append`, `status`, `releasable`, `adopt`.
- `hooks/` — the hooks listed under Hooks; `hooks/_hook_common.sh` is their sourced skeleton.
